defs.def: an event, an action, a fact, etc. that shows that sth exists, is happening or may happen in the future 迹象；征兆；预兆

ex.s: She searched the faces of her classmates for signs of panic.
ex.t: 当某事与他们的观点矛盾时，他们不会将其视为例外。

ex.s: Bonds, who bought his first cattle almost 50 years ago, still has each of his cowboys inspect 300 or 400 cattle daily and look for signs that an animal is getting sick.
ex.t: 邦德在近50年前购买了他的第一头牛，他仍然让每个牛仔每天检查300或400头牛，并寻找动物生病的迹象。

ex.s: This is how everyone learned to read． We would start off with sentences， then paragraphs， and then stories． It seemed an unending journey， but even as a six﹣year﹣old girl I realized that knowing how to read could open many doors． When mom said， "The C﹣A﹣N﹣D﹣Y is hidden on the top shelf，" I knew where the candy was． My progress in reading raised my curiosity， and I wanted to know everything． I often found myself telling my mom to drive more slowly， so that I could read all of the road signs we passed．
ex.t: 每个人都是这样学会阅读的。我们从句子开始，然后是段落，再然后是故事。这似乎是一段永无止境的旅程，但即使作为一个六岁的女孩，我也意识到学会阅读能打开许多扇门。当妈妈说：“C-A-N-D-Y藏在最上面的架子上”时，我知道糖果在哪里。我在阅读上的进步激发了我的好奇心，我想知道一切。我经常叫妈妈开慢一点，这样我就能读出我们路过的所有路标。

ex.s: （2）According to Paragraph 3， the author's reading of road signs indicates     ．
ex.t: （2）根据第3段，作者对路标的阅读表明____。

ex.s: It is also said that mice and snakes head for safer ground several days before an earthquake, while dogs avoiding the beach may be a sign that a tsunami is approaching.
ex.t: 还有人说，老鼠和蛇会在地震前几天逃往更安全的地方，而狗避开海滩可能是海啸即将来临的征兆。

ex.s: Over generations, communities became desensitised to increasingly smelly rivers, a sign of broader ecosystem degradation.
ex.t: 一代代下来，这些社区对越来越臭的河流变得麻木，这是更广泛的生态系统退化的一个信号。

ex.s: They use their noses to assess their environment and look out for any signs of danger.
ex.t: 它们用鼻子来评估周围环境，并留意任何危险的迹象。

ex.s: In most people the first signs show up in their 50s or early 60s.
ex.t: 对于大多数人来说，最初的症状出现在50多岁或60岁出头。
